messages:
jordan: Heads-up — EU promo spike over the past 3h. short-chat QPS ~2.4x baseline, p99 token latency on the hot path up from ~280ms -> ~480ms. Notified because admit is starting to drop tail SLAs.

autoscaler-bot: [metric snapshot] eu-west-1: GPU util 92%, queue depth 134, avg tokens per req 58, lossy-drop=12/min

alex: Thanks. Quick read: request mix shifted to short sessions (avg tokens down) but arrival bursts are tighter so batching can't amortize. We're saturating kv-cache lookups + kernel slots.

maria: Can we do an admission bias towards small-seq requests? e.g., favor seq<=128 so we keep p99 for interactive flows. Also want numbers on how many extra GPUs we'd need to hold p99 if we instead scaled linearly.

jordan: Rough calc I did: observed arrival λ_peak ≈ 165 req/s. avg tokens ≈ 58. A single GPU model hotpath throughput ≈ 220 tokens/s => per-GPU req service rate µ ≈ 220/58 ≈ 3.8 req/s. So GPUs needed ≈ λ/µ ≈ 165/3.8 ≈ 44 GPUs. Baseline we're at 28 GPUs, so ~+16 GPUs required for headroom.

alex: I re-ran with p99 safety margin (x1.25 for burstiness): 44 * 1.25 ≈ 55 -> add ~27 GPUs. That's the worst-case immediate burn. If we did soft-admit (drop or queue long seqs) we only need ~+10 GPUs.

maria: Cost check: our committed pool unit cost ~"$2.15/GPU-hour" for these instances. If we add 10 GPUs for a 6-hour window that's 10 * 6 * 2.15 = $129. If we add 27 GPUs it's 27 * 6 * 2.15 = $348. low-touch mitigation seems cheaper.

leena: Operational mitigations we can flip quickly:
- enable per-route admit policy (canary to eu-west-1) to prefer seq<=128
- increase KV cache TTL for short prompt keys to reduce redundant memory ops
- pre-warm 4 GPUs with cached kernels for the hot model variant

Snippet to toggle admit (ops CLI):
```
opsctl admit set --region eu-west-1 --route chat.hot --policy soft --bias small_seq:0.85 --ttl 10m
```

sam: I can push the admit canary now to 10% traffic and monitor p99. If green, ramp to 50% over 10m, then to 100%. Also enabling burst-dedicated for 20 GPUs as interim.

jordan: TL;DR proposed hybrid plan: A) Immediately canary soft-admit into eu-west-1 at 10% for seq>128 bias, B) pre-warm 4 GPUs and increase KV TTL, C) request 20 GPUs burst from dedicated pool as emergency fallback.

alex: Addendum: We should also enable fallback routing for long-form customers to lower-capacity model variant (quantized-q4a) to avoid hard drops. Tiny code snippet for routing rule: 
```
routing: if seq>1024 and admit==deny -> route: model-small-q4a, priority: best-effort
```

maria: I'll own a quick cost/runbook doc and estimate hours. Will post expected GPU-hour delta and cost per hour. For now, provisional numbers: 20 GPU 3h burst -> 60 GPU-hours -> ~$129. (I used $2.15/hr)

leena: I'm on prewarm and KV TTL. pushing patch to infra now.

sam: Canary started (10%). autoscaler-bot will post p95/p99 every 60s.

autoscaler-bot: canary=10% green? p95=110ms (stable), p99=320ms -> improved from 480ms but still above 300ms target. queue depth down 27%.

jordan: Good improvement. If p99 stays <=350ms at 10%, ramp to 50% and keep burst capacity in reserve.

alex: Filing a follow-up to model-ops: can we add a lightweight short-session optimized variant permanently? This will reduce future headroom needs.

maria: Agreed. Action items: Jordan (lead rollout), Leena (prewarm + TTL), Sam (canary & burst), Alex (fallback routing + model-ops ticket), Maria (cost doc + post-mortem). Will reconvene in 45m or sooner. :thumbsup:
